standard.title: Choreograph dance sequences
standard.description: use the elements of dance to choreograph dance sequences
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have created arts works communicating ideas and used play and imagination to discover movement possibilities (Foundation). They can sequence simple movement ideas and present them to peers.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students use the elements of dance to choreograph dance sequences.

nodes.label: Elements of dance as tools
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and intentionally use at least two elements of dance (e.g. space, time, dynamics) as tools for shaping movement.
nodes.minimum_width: Using one or two elements (e.g. level and direction) deliberately in movement — can name the element being used.
nodes.typical_width: Exploring and naming how space (level, direction, size), time (speed, rhythm), and dynamics (heavy/light, sharp/smooth) shape movement; using these elements intentionally in short movement improvisations.
wider: Use music created by students themselves (rhythmic patterns, clapping) as a prompt — applying time and dynamics elements in response
Explore how maintaining balance, manipulating posture, or isolating specific body parts are themselves expressive element choices
nodes.hinge_reason: Without a working vocabulary of dance elements as intentional tools, students cannot make deliberate choreographic choices in N2-N3. They will move without compositional awareness.

response_modes.reason: Students need vocabulary and labelling before they can use elements as tools. Name elements in the moment during play: 'You just changed your level — that's a space choice.' Use Viewpoints-style questioning to build metacognitive awareness.

success_criteria: Student can name at least two elements of dance
Student can demonstrate a movement choice that deliberately uses one named element (e.g. 'I'm going low — that's level')

nodes.label: Improvising and selecting movement
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can improvise movement using the elements of dance and select movements they want to use in a sequence.
nodes.minimum_width: Improvising a movement sequence in response to a stimulus; selecting two or more movements to keep and sequence.
nodes.typical_width: Using improvisation to generate a range of movement possibilities in response to stimuli (weather, music, stories, environments); selecting, sharing and learning movements with a partner; combining ideas to extend sequences.
wider: Improvise locomotor sequences (travelling movements) and teach these to a partner — combining and extending into a collaborative sequence
Use imagery (floating like a cloud, stomping like a giant) as stimulus — selecting movements that best represent the image

response_modes.reason: Improvisation requires a physical and imaginative repertoire. Students who have encountered many different stimuli types and movement contexts will generate richer ideas during improvisation.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Students who improvise across diverse stimulus types — movement, music, imagery, nature, story — develop genuine choreographic imagination rather than defaulting to a fixed set of familiar moves.
success_criteria: Student generates multiple movement possibilities in an improvisation (does not stop at the first idea)
Student can identify which movements they want to keep and use in their sequence

nodes.label: Choreographing and refining a sequence
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can choreograph a dance sequence with a beginning, middle and end, using the elements of dance, and can reflect on and refine it using peer/teacher feedback.
nodes.minimum_width: A choreographed sequence with clear start and end; at least two identifiable element choices; can describe what the sequence is communicating.
nodes.typical_width: A dance sequence that represents an idea (weather, place, story, music) using multiple element choices; devised starting shape, locomotor movement through space, and ending position; combined with a partner or group to extend the sequence; feedback sought and used to refine.
wider: Choreograph a sequence that communicates care for a place that is important to the student — using element choices to express relationship and responsibility
Devise a collaborative sequence where each person's contribution is identifiable — using contrast and connection between individual parts
nodes.hinge_reason: Completing a choreographed sequence — with intentional element use and reflective refinement — is the prerequisite for all subsequent Creating strand work. Students who have not produced a whole sequence lack the foundational production experience.

response_modes.reason: Choreographing integrates element knowledge (N1) with improvised material (N2) into a structured, communicative whole. Scaffold with structural prompts: 'How will it begin?', 'How do you move through the space?', 'How does it end?'

success_criteria: Student produces a dance sequence with a beginning, middle and end
Student can identify at least two element choices in their sequence
Student can describe what their sequence communicates and incorporate at least one piece of feedback
